rows.evidence: Rust induction replay over one tracked AgentRewardBench slice.
rows.main_numbers: 729 operations; 15 induced stacks; depth histogram 2:1/3:1/4:13; session-as-evidence view has 16 stacks.
rows.non_claim: Not automatic discovery of all intent boundaries.
rows.question: Can the profiler form recursive operation stacks without a user-supplied field chain?
rows.supported_conclusion: Visible boundary evidence can induce ragged operation-only stacks, and session remains optional evidence.

rows.evidence: The induced view is scored on the same six R300/R320 labeled tasks as the main benchmark.
rows.main_numbers: 4/6 variable-depth tasks, 2/6 material-stop tasks; AP 0.2762 vs hand-configured 0.3116; work@5 0.653 vs flat 1; groups 12 vs fixed-session 285.
rows.non_claim: Not a replacement for task-specific profile specs.
rows.question: Do induced stacks work as a visible profiler view on real hidden-label tasks?
rows.supported_conclusion: Induction reduces flat work and fixed-session fragmentation, but hand-configured specs remain stronger by AP.

rows.evidence: The depth cap is swept from 1 to 5 while hidden labels are used only after profiling.
rows.main_numbers: best query-aware median AP at depth 3 (0.2865); lowest median work@5 at depth 5 (0.4727); material-split AP-best depths span 2, 3, 4, 5.
rows.non_claim: Not an automatic depth selector or analyst-productivity result.
rows.question: Is induced-stack depth a real tuning surface?
rows.supported_conclusion: Different objectives prefer different recursive depths, so depth is a profile-configuration knob.
